questions.prompt: How many Hail Marys are in a traditional Rosary decade?
options: Ten
Five
Twelve
questions.explanation: A traditional decade contains ten Hail Marys while you meditate on one mystery. Ave Maria also offers shorter family forms.

questions.prompt: In the Rosary, what is a mystery?
options: A prayer kept secret from others
An event in the life of Jesus or Mary to contemplate
The number of beads remaining
questions.explanation: A mystery gives your reflection a focus, such as the Annunciation or the Resurrection. It is not a riddle to solve.

questions.prompt: When praying alone, how should you use the app's Leader and Response parts?
options: Read only Leader
Read only Response
You may read both parts
questions.explanation: Leader and Response divide the words for a group. When you pray alone, you may say both.

questions.prompt: In the Milk lesson, what moves while you close and relax your hand?
options: Your whole forearm pumps up and down
The hand closes while the forearm stays still
Both arms swing outward
questions.explanation: Start with a curved hand, close it into a fist, then relax. Keep the movement in the hand.

questions.prompt: For the More sign taught in Tiny Signs, what meets?
options: The two gathered groups of fingertips
The palms in a clap
The backs of the hands
questions.explanation: Gather each hand's fingertips to its thumb. Bring those two fingertip groups together in front of your chest.

questions.prompt: In the All done lesson, how do your open palms turn?
options: From forward to facing each other
From up to down near your waist
From facing you to facing forward
questions.explanation: Keep both hands open at chest height and turn the wrists outward together. Your arms do not need to wave.

questions.prompt: Before finalizing godparent arrangements, who should confirm sponsor eligibility and required forms?
options: The person taking the family photos
The app's checklist automatically
Your parish
questions.explanation: The Faith plan asks you to confirm preparation and godparent eligibility with your parish. Save its specific instructions.

questions.prompt: Who can offer the simple daily child blessing described in the Playbook?
options: A parent
Only a priest at church
Only the godparents on the Baptism anniversary
questions.explanation: The USCCB blessing is a family practice a parent can offer, including before bed: 'May God bless you.'

questions.prompt: Which action most directly models forgiveness for your child?
options: Asking your child to recite a rule about forgiveness
Acknowledging your own mistake, apologizing, and making it right
Waiting until your child can explain forgiveness
questions.explanation: The Playbook starts with the adults' example. Your child can see what an apology and repair look like in ordinary life.

questions.prompt: In the Annunciation reflection, who brings the announcement to Mary?
options: The Angel Gabriel
Elizabeth
Saint Joseph
questions.explanation: The first Joyful Mystery recalls Gabriel announcing that Mary would become the Mother of God.

questions.prompt: Whom does Mary visit in the second Joyful Mystery?
options: Martha
Elizabeth
Mary Magdalene
questions.explanation: The Visitation focuses on Mary visiting Elizabeth. The app connects this mystery with charity toward your neighbor.

questions.prompt: Which Joyful Mystery reflects on Jesus' birth at Bethlehem?
options: The Presentation
The Finding in the Temple
The Nativity
questions.explanation: The Nativity is the third Joyful Mystery. Its reflection centers on the Infant Jesus in the manger.

questions.prompt: For Mom, where does the thumb of your open hand touch or come close?
options: Your forehead
Your chin
Your chest
questions.explanation: In the Mom lesson, the open hand's thumb comes to the chin. Dad uses the forehead.

questions.prompt: Which handshape and location match Dad in Tiny Signs?
options: An open hand with the thumb near the forehead
A closed fist beside the cheek
An open hand with the thumb near the chin
questions.explanation: Spread the fingers comfortably and bring your thumb to your forehead. Use a small, clear contact.

questions.prompt: For Help, a thumb-up fist rests on your other palm. What happens next?
options: The fist lifts away from the palm
The supporting hand turns palm-down
Both connected hands lift together
questions.explanation: The supporting palm faces up. Keep the hands touching as you lift them together.

questions.prompt: After saving a handoff, how do you get that snapshot to the other parent?
options: It automatically syncs to their phone
Refresh the page on both phones
Use Copy saved handoff, then share the copied text
questions.explanation: The current Playbook saves details in this browser. Copying provides text you can send or otherwise share yourself.

questions.prompt: Which entry makes the next parent's handoff most useful?
options: The actual last event time and a brief relevant note
Only the time you hope tomorrow's event will happen
A general daily average with no recent details
questions.explanation: The handoff has separate last-feed, last-diaper, and last-sleep times, plus notes about what helped and what comes next.

questions.prompt: What does the Playbook mean by 'Own the whole job'?
options: Wait for the other parent to assign every small step
Agree on practical care, settling, and who gets the next rest block
Take responsibility only for recording the handoff
questions.explanation: A useful shift agreement includes the practical work and protecting rest. The app also reminds you to support the recovering parent.

questions.prompt: Which event opens the Luminous Mysteries?
options: Jesus' Baptism in the Jordan
Jesus' birth in Bethlehem
The Resurrection
questions.explanation: The first Luminous Mystery is the Baptism in the Jordan, followed by the Wedding at Cana.

questions.prompt: Which Luminous Mystery includes Mary's instruction to do whatever Jesus tells the servants?
options: The Transfiguration
The Wedding at Cana
The Proclamation of the Kingdom
questions.explanation: The Cana reflection connects Mary's words to trust in her intercession and attention to Jesus.

questions.prompt: Which event is the fifth Luminous Mystery?
options: The Finding in the Temple
The Ascension
The Institution of the Eucharist
questions.explanation: This final Luminous Mystery reflects on Jesus giving himself in the Eucharist.

questions.prompt: In the Sleep lesson, how does the hand change as it lowers past the face?
options: It stays in a tight fist
The open fingers gather to the thumb
It changes from a fist to two pointing fingers
questions.explanation: Begin with an open hand facing you, then lower it while gathering the fingertips to the thumb. Finish with a flattened O, not a tight fist.

questions.prompt: Where are both hands placed for the Diaper sign taught in the app?
options: At the two sides of your lower waist
Above the forehead
At the center of the upper chest
questions.explanation: Both hands tap the index and middle fingers to their thumbs near the sides of the waist, like fastening diaper tabs.

questions.prompt: For Eat, where do the gathered fingertips move?
options: To the forehead
To the shoulder
To the mouth
questions.explanation: Gather your fingertips and thumb together, then bring them to the mouth in one small movement.

questions.prompt: For a toddler learning a limit, which response matches the Playbook?
options: Repeat a long explanation until they agree
Change the limit whenever they protest
Use a few calm words, follow through, and show what they can do
questions.explanation: The Playbook recommends clear, consistent limits and an example of the acceptable action. Toddlers are still learning self-control.

questions.prompt: Which is the Playbook's example of a manageable toddler helping job?
options: Put one toy in a basket together
Sort and organize every toy independently
Take over the whole cleanup without help
questions.explanation: Start with a small, safe contribution. Work alongside your child and let them do the part they can.

questions.prompt: Your toddler tries a manageable block-building challenge. Which response best matches 'try again' practice?
options: Immediately rebuild it for them every time
Notice the effort and offer enough help to continue
Require them to finish before taking any break
questions.explanation: The aim is practice with support: allow an attempt, give a useful hint, and recognize effort. A break is allowed when frustration grows.

questions.prompt: In the Hail Mary, what do we ask Mary to do for us?
options: Pray for us sinners
Give us our daily bread
Send forth the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: The prayer asks the Mother of God to pray for us now and at the hour of our death.

questions.prompt: In the Our Father, our request for forgiveness is paired with what action toward others?
options: Remembering the day's mystery
Forgiving those who trespass against us
Choosing the next Rosary decade
questions.explanation: The prayer connects asking for God's forgiveness with forgiving others.

questions.prompt: Which common prayer in Ave Maria begins by asking God to bless us and the gifts we are about to receive?
options: The Memorare
The Guardian Angel Prayer
Grace Before Meals
questions.explanation: Grace Before Meals gives thanks for God's gifts before eating. You can find it in the app's Common prayers list.

questions.prompt: Which fingers are extended for the Water handshape taught in Tiny Signs?
options: Thumb and little finger
Index, middle, and ring fingers
Index finger only
questions.explanation: Extend the index, middle, and ring fingers while the thumb holds the little finger down. The hand taps near the chin.

questions.prompt: When opening your hands for Book, which edges stay together?
options: The little-finger edges
The thumb tips only
The wrists with fingers pointing down
questions.explanation: Start palm to palm, then open the palms upward like book covers while keeping the little-finger edges connected.

questions.prompt: Which movement matches Drink in the app?
options: Tap a straight index finger beside the chin
Close a curved hand into a fist at chest height
Arc a C-shaped hand toward the mouth like tipping a cup
questions.explanation: Keep the imaginary-cup shape as the hand moves toward the mouth. This differs from Milk's opening and closing movement.

questions.prompt: Before leaving for Mass with your baby, what does the Playbook suggest agreeing on?
options: A score for how quietly the baby sits
Who will avoid all care interruptions
Who carries the bag and handles changes or a settling break
questions.explanation: A small plan helps both parents share the practical work. Prepare for ordinary care needs while participating in family worship.

questions.prompt: How does the Playbook suggest beginning a Bible story with an infant?
options: Use a calm, awake moment and keep it short
Finish a full chapter regardless of their attention
Wait until they can answer questions about the story
questions.explanation: Read with a warm voice and simple words. End when your baby needs a different activity; this is shared family time.

questions.prompt: Which practice fits the Playbook's way of introducing gratitude?
options: Ask the toddler for a perfect spoken thank-you every time
Model a specific thank-you and invite a word, sign, or wave
Delay family gratitude until the child can memorize a prayer
questions.explanation: Start by demonstrating gratitude yourself. Invite participation in a form your child can manage.
